record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Can split learning be parallelized effectively on resource-constrained edge devices so that different parts of the split computation can run with lower centralized training time while remaining practical in federated deployments?

evidence.quote: However, it is still an open question to explore such parallelization of split learning on edge devices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a neural network model M with L layers is trained collaboratively by a central server S and a collection of N resource-constrained edge devices D_1,...,D_N (each device having limited compute, memory, and bandwidth, and holding a private local dataset). In split learning, the model M is partitioned at a designated cut layer ℓ into a client-side sub-model M_c (layers 1,...,ℓ) executed on each edge device and a server-side sub-model M_s (layers ℓ+1,...,L) executed on S, with forward activations at layer ℓ and backward gradients exchanged between device and server. In its standard formulation, devices interact with the server sequentially, so that the centralized training time scales roughly linearly with N.

Design a parallelized variant of split learning satisfying all of the following requirements, or prove that no such variant exists:

(a) Multiple devices D_i may execute their forward and backward passes on M_c concurrently and the server may process the corresponding server-side computations on M_s in parallel, so that the total wall-clock training time per global epoch is sublinear in N (ideally O(1) up to communication and aggregation costs).

(b) The per-device computation, memory footprint, and communication volume per round remain within the budget of resource-constrained edge devices, independent of N.

(c) The trained global model achieves accuracy comparable (within a specified tolerance ε > 0) to that obtained by sequential split learning on the same data and architecture.

(d) The privacy properties of split learning (i.e., raw data never leaves any device D_i) are preserved.

Specify the protocol explicitly, including how client-side sub-model weights are synchronized across devices, how the server schedules and aggregates parallel activations and gradients, and provide a convergence analysis together with bounds on the centralized training time, communication cost, and accuracy gap relative to the sequential baseline.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple subsequent works have proposed parallelized split-learning frameworks for resource-constrained edge devices, including SplitFed/SFL, CPSL (cluster-based parallel SL), EdgeSplit, HSFL, and ParallelSFL. These frameworks demonstrate empirically that parallelization is feasible and reduces wall-clock training time while preserving privacy and approximate accuracy. However, fully general theoretical guarantees on convergence, optimal cut-layer selection, and tight communication/computation/accuracy trade-offs under arbitrary device heterogeneity remain active research directions, so the broad open question is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Split Federated Learning Over Heterogeneous Edge Devices: Algorithm and Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Split Federated Learning combines ideas of split learning and federated learning to parallelize training across heterogeneous edge devices.
status_evidence.claim: Parallelized split learning frameworks for heterogeneous edge devices have been proposed and analyzed.

status_evidence.title: Resource-efficient Parallel Split Learning in Heterogeneous Edge Computing
status_evidence.snippet: EdgeSplit adaptively segments the model into varying depths to enhance training efficiency on less powerful edge devices.
status_evidence.claim: Parallel split learning has been shown effective on resource-constrained edge devices.

status_evidence.title: ParallelSFL: A Novel Split Federated Learning Framework Tackling Heterogeneity Issues
status_evidence.snippet: ParallelSFL splits the model into bottom and top submodels and clusters workers to perform SFL in parallel, reducing communication bottlenecks.
status_evidence.claim: Recent frameworks parallelize split learning to reduce centralized training time.
